description: Replace the remaining n2048 compact-WY projection, shared-T triangular solve, and baddbmm application chain with a fused panel apply: stage T once per matrix, stream V^TQ tiles through warp-specialized shared memory, solve in registers, and accumulate Q -= VY using tensor cores or strict FP32 as certificate margins require; preserve strict A*Q/certificate, ownership, fallbacks, and portability.

Fused each n2048 compact-WY projection and application into a TF32x3 16-column strip kernel that retains projected tiles in shared memory while keeping the proven shared-T factor solve. Kernelguard was clean and validation passed 39/39, but n2048 measured 262448.540 us and aggregate 25200.958 us because the irregular final row was included in a 16-row WMMA tile, corrupting adjacent storage and driving certificate fallback. Nsys recorded 17.008 ms across 64 fused launches plus cuSOLVER fallback kernels.

Moved every odd-height n2048 panel's final row out of WMMA and into exact scalar cleanup, eliminating the out-of-slice write and certificate fallback from trial 0. Kernelguard remained clean and validation passed 39/39. Aggregate recovered to 23003.404 us and n2048 to 82131.808 us, still above parent 74136.576. Nsys measured the fused kernel at 18.746 ms over eight profiled calls and the retained solve at 3.215 ms; batch-8 strip replication remains the next measured target.

Widened each fused n2048 projection/apply CTA from 16 to 64 columns, reusing one panel and factor fragment across four output tiles and reducing CTA count fourfold. The extension built and Kernelguard passed, but official validation reached n2048 then surfaced an asynchronous CUDA invalid-argument launch error before refinement; the four live WMMA accumulator tiles at 512 threads exceeded the viable launch resource envelope. No benchmark metric was recorded.

Retried wider fused WY strips at 32 columns after resetting the failed 64-column trial. Two live accumulator tiles fit the 512-thread launch; panel and factor fragments are reused across both outputs, halving CTA count and duplicated operand reads. Kernelguard was clean and validation passed 39/39. Aggregate measured 23004.084 us and n2048 82110.713 us, effectively unchanged from the valid 16-column trial at 23003.404/82131.808.

Reduced the valid 32-column fused projection/apply from three-term TF32x3 to single-pass TF32, relying on the existing tensor-high Newton step and strict A*Q certificate. Kernelguard was clean; validation passed 39/39 with n2048 scaled residual 3.56 and orthogonality 3.8. Aggregate improved to 22965.499 us and n2048 to 79865.382 us. Nsys measured fused work at 11.846 ms over eight calls versus 18.746 ms for TF32x3; solve remained 3.222 ms.

Retested 64-column fused WY strips after single-pass TF32 removed all low-part fragments. Build and Kernelguard passed, but n2048 validation again surfaced an asynchronous CUDA invalid-argument launch error before refinement. Four accumulator tiles at 512 threads remain outside the viable kernel resource envelope even without TF32x3; no benchmark metric was recorded.

Implemented the complete fused panel apply requested by the brief: each CTA stages all packed upper T tiles once, computes V^TQ into shared memory, solves 16-row factor tiles through T in warp registers, and accumulates Q -= VY with single-pass TF32; no factor or projection tensor is materialized. Kernelguard was clean and validation passed 39/39. Repeating the sequential solve across 32-column CTAs raised n2048 to 409127.899 us and aggregate to 26039.046 us.

Consolidated the n2048 compact-WY projection, proven shared-T solve, and baddbmm apply behind one extension call while preserving optimized library GEMMs, exact arithmetic, per-call factor/projection ownership, certificates, and all fallbacks. Kernelguard was clean and validation passed 39/39. N2048 measured 74249.458 us versus parent 74136.576, while cross-shape noise put aggregate at 22868.753 us versus parent 22850.591.

After the library projection completes, ran the shared-T solve in place over the current panel's now-dead reflector columns and applied that strided factor with cuBLAS, eliminating the separate factor allocation while preserving one solve per panel. Kernelguard was clean and validation passed 39/39. Aggregate measured a brief-best 22825.413 us; n2048 was 74186.792 us, effectively tied with parent 74136.576 under the stated 1% noise floor.

Scoped medium float32 matmul precision to the in-place-factor WY projection/application while restoring the caller precision before Newton refinement and the strict A*Q certificate. Kernelguard was clean and validation passed 39/39 with unchanged residuals. N2048 measured 74144.417 us and aggregate 22827.199 us, tied with the high-precision in-place trial. Nsys confirmed PyTorch selected tcgen05 TF32 kernels in both modes; solve totaled 3.249 ms over 64 launches.

Allocated one per-call [batch,256,2048] projection workspace and reused width-narrowed views across all eight n2048 panels, while retaining in-place reflector factors and tcgen05 library products. Kernelguard was clean and validation passed 39/39. Aggregate reached a new brief-best 22811.354 us; n2048 measured 74181.437 us, still tied with parent and the prior in-place trials within noise.

Moved the entire eight-panel n2048 backtransform loop into one extension call, preserving high-precision Gram formation, medium/tcgen05 projection and apply, one reusable projection workspace, in-place reflector factors, strict downstream certification, and per-call ownership. Kernelguard was clean and validation passed 39/39. N2048 measured 74207.497 us and aggregate 22837.472 us, showing no measurable benefit over the Python-loop workspace trial.

Final replay of selected e3654f70: one per-call projection workspace reused across eight panels, in-place reflector factors, medium/tcgen05 library projection and apply, strict downstream A*Q/certificate, and no change to other routes. Kernelguard was clean and validation passed 39/39. Replay measured 22850.211 us aggregate and 74211.642 us n2048; the same source previously measured 22811.354/74181.437. Final nsys records reducer 60.816 ms/call, solve 3.249 ms over 64 launches, and tcgen05 TF32 panel GEMMs.

Completed 13 measured trials (11 succeeded, two logged validation failures) across custom and library-backed n2048 compact-WY fusion. Terminal e3654f70bacdaa2e86ffac6ccddd8ffdfe9e1ca1 reuses one per-call [batch,256,2048] projection workspace across all panels, computes projection before safely overwriting each now-dead reflector panel with its shared-T factor, and retains Blackwell tcgen05 TF32 library application plus strict downstream A*Q/certificate and all other routes. It is Kernelguard-clean and passes 39/39. The same source measured 22811.354 us aggregate/74181.437 us n2048, then final replay 22850.211/74211.642 versus parent 22850.591/74136.576, all target deltas within the 1% noise floor. Final nsys brief-70-trial-12-e3654f70... records reducer 60.816 ms/call, 64 solve launches totaling 3.249 ms, and tcgen05 TF32 panel GEMMs. Built custom fusion evidence: corrected TF32x3 projection/apply measured 82131.808 us n2048; 32-column operand reuse measured 82110.713; single-pass TF32 improved it to 79865.382; 64-column four-accumulator variants failed launch and were logged; the full requested packed-T/register-solve/on-chip-projection fused kernel passed 39/39 but repeated its sequential solve per output strip and measured 409127.899 us. Consolidated library dispatch measured 74249.458; in-place factor reuse 74186.792; medium and high both selected tcgen05 and measured 74144.417/74186.792; moving the whole panel loop into C++ measured 74207.497. Keep the search moving: a CUTLASS/tcgen05 fused mainloop with TMA instead of legacy WMMA, cluster-distributed shared factor tiles so one register solve feeds several output strips, contiguous factor leasing from already-consumed reflector regions, and targeted certificate stress for single-pass tensor arithmetic remain concrete extensions. No leaderboard submission was made by this worker, and no account leaderboard score is attributed to it.

Replace the remaining n2048 compact-WY projection, shared-T triangular solve, and baddbmm application chain with a fused panel apply: stage T once per matrix, stream V^TQ tiles through warp-specialized shared memory, solve in registers, and accumulate Q -= VY using tensor cores or strict FP32 as certificate margins require; preserve strict A*Q/certificate, ownership, fallbacks, and portability.

Replaced the two WY library GEMMs with a persistent Triton/tcgen05 program per 64-column strip: each program forms V^TQ in tensor memory and reuses it across all 32-row output tiles, while the shared-T factor solve runs once globally. Kernelguard was clean and validation passed 39/39, but benchmark n2048 measured 258487.895 us and aggregate 25146.623. Nsys shows the fused kernel itself only 12.265 ms over eight calls and solve 3.247 ms; single-pass TF32 failed the benchmark certificate and triggered a full cuSOLVER fallback dominated by 14,336 symv plus tens of thousands of gemv kernels.

Switched both persistent tcgen05 products to TF32x3. Kernelguard was clean and validation passed 39/39; benchmark certification stayed on the custom path, reducing n2048 from the single-pass fallback's 258487.895 us to 80232.508 us, with aggregate 22981.982 us. Nsys measures the fused dataflow at 24.585 ms over eight calls and the one-per-panel factor solve at 3.227 ms; no cuSOLVER symv/gemv fallback appears.

Widened the persistent tcgen05 tile to 64 output rows by 128 columns to increase panel/factor reuse and halve program count. Build and Kernelguard passed, but Triton rejected the first n2048 launch before execution: generated shared-memory demand was 335872 bytes versus the B200 hardware limit of 232448. No benchmark metric was recorded.

Kept TF32x3 for V^TQ projection but reduced the factor-times-projection application to single-pass TF32. Kernelguard was clean and validation passed 39/39; benchmark stayed on the custom path and n2048 improved from all-TF32x3 80232.508 us to 76701.861 us, with aggregate 22904.703 us. Test-shape scaled residual/orthogonality rose from 1.70/2.54 to 4.84/5.74 but remained inside the strict checker.
